summary: Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Osaka, Otani, and Yale universities, supervised by Noritoshi Aramaki and Stanley Weinstein. He was appointed professor at Waseda University in 2015.

Nobuyuki Kaji is a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. His career includes posts at Koyasan, Nagoya, and Tamkang universities, as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College, and director at Ritsumeikan University.

Nobuyuki Matsumoto works in the field of history and archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Waseda University under Shinya Hoshiyama and served as a researcher at the Kuboso Memorial Museum of Arts, Izumi (attested 1986).

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University (~1989–2007) and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).
Nobuyuki Yamagiwa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki, later serving at Otani University as an assistant (1976), lecturer (1986), and Buddhist studies laboratory appointee (~1990–2011).

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. She studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914) and held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).
Norbert Brox was a scholar of religious studies and history and archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1969–1978) and the University of Regensburg (~1978–2000).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines, later holding professorships at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi, later serving as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011).

Noriaki Hosoda is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He held assistant and associate professor posts at Hokkaido University (attested 1986, 2003) and served as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there (attested 1982).

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku, Bukkyo, and Visva-Bharati universities. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving successively as lecturer, associate professor, and professor from 1976 until becoming professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).

Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda, later becoming a professor at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Norio Fujisawa was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950). He held a post at Kyoto University (~1966–1989) and later served as director of the Kyoto National Museum (~1992–2001).
Norio Harada is a sinologist who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1964).
Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

Noriyuki Kudo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed postgraduate study at Bukkyo University. He has held positions at Bukkyo University, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, where he became a professor.
